title: Converting an enumeration to and from a string
recap: Enum-to-text conversion gives a domain value a user-facing name; text-to-enum conversion must also describe invalid input. An optional makes an unrecognized string distinct from every valid color.
Keep a precise normalization policy. Case sensitivity and whitespace rules must be stated rather than guessed by callers.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Practice converting an enumeration to and from a string.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement colorName(color) and parseColor(text). Names are exactly lowercase "red", "green", "blue". parseColor returns an engaged optional<Color> for those names, otherwise nullopt; no whitespace trimming or case folding. colorName receives valid enumerators only. Returning string_view literals is safe because their storage lasts for the program.
hints: A switch can map enumerators to static string literals.
Compare text contents against each accepted name.
Do not use a valid color as the parse-error result.
